svg.title: Metadata-driven database-source flow from BRD to script generation
svg.desc: A production architecture flow chart showing target-resident metadata selection, one-time onboarding, the common BRD and design flow, database discovery, metadata drafting and approval, and target-specific script generation. Execution is outside scope.
svg.text: Complete design-time flow: BRD → approved metadata → target-specific script artifact (execution excluded)
Source type = DATABASE • Select target = Databricks, Snowflake, or Fabric
Physical metadata I/O branches here; logical workflow stays common
1. One-time platform bootstrap — create/verify exactly eight tables
4 configuration tables + 4 runtime/control tables in the selected target platform
Idempotent, versioned platform migration • no dynamic DDL inside ingestion jobs
JDBC contract and secret references — never secret values
Capture business outcomes, entities, measures, constraints and target expectations
BRD is not forced into the eight ingestion tables
Resolve business terminology, required datasets, SLAs and governance needs
Identify measures, dimensions, facts, candidate grain and source entities
Approve the business intent before technical metadata is generated
Select candidate databases, schemas, tables and queries required by the BRD
Schemas • tables/views • columns/types • PK/FK • row counts
Watermark candidates • partition candidates • CDC capabilities
Normalize JDBC discovery into one source-neutral dataset and schema model
Nulls, uniqueness, patterns, PII, semantic types, key confidence and relationships
One independently retryable object per stage and target
No draft is executable until validation and atomic activation
Source contract, target, write mode, validation, dependencies
Mappings, casts, business keys, facts/dimensions, joins, aggregates and DQ rules
The LLM proposes metadata; it does not activate or execute it
Relationships • fields/types • merge keys • grain • dependencies • transformations
Reject unsafe SQL, incomplete Gold inputs, mixed versions and invalid target names
New version ACTIVE • previous version SUPERSEDED • no partial mapping set
Calculate configuration, mapping-set and complete snapshot hashes
Rejected version never replaces current active version
Only INCREMENTAL, CDC or other stateful Source→Bronze objects
Committed initial value • version 0 • checkpoint scope
Platform-neutral source, mappings, targets, validation and Gold dependency plan
This is the final fully common logical artifact
No target-specific syntax in the canonical plan
Syntax • identifiers • key coverage • dependency completeness • secret scan
Persist artifact URI, hash, generator version and metadata snapshot hash
Do not store large scripts or credentials in metadata
RUNTIME HANDOFF — intentionally outside this diagram
ctl_ingestion_queue, ctl_run and ctl_error_log begin here; ctl_watermark is updated only after successful target commits
Common logical workflow • target-resident metadata from the first operation • database-specific discovery in the middle • target-specific compilation at the end
